items.title: [Engine] Windows/WDDM: parked-conversation snapshot copies corrupt at 262144 -> all-logits NaN (#879 symptom, separate trigger)
items.body:
### Area

Engine

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Terminal (`serve/server.py` + engine); the fix is built from source.

### What happened

With `--kv int8 --max-context 262144 --expert-cache auto` and the default checkpoints/prompt cache, after roughly 6–10 unique prompts have parked, the engine logs

```
checkpoint save: conversation snapshot running-state copy: invalid argument
```

and every later request fails with "the model's output became non-finite (NaN)". Same config at `--max-context 196608`: clean. Same 262144 with `--prompt-cache 0`: clean. The same model files and settings on Linux on this PC: clean. A reference PC with the same GPU, driver and Windows runs this config on auto without problems, so this is the allocation map on this machine, not a broken driver.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

1. Windows 11, RX 9070 XT, Strata 0.2.0-beta, IQ3_S model.
2. `serve/server.py --engine strata --port 1235 --config <cfg>` with engine args `--kv int8 --max-context 262144 --expert-cache auto --spec 4` (default checkpoints/prompt cache, tuning table `tools/hip/gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt`).
3. Send 11 unique ~1.5k-token prompts sequentially.

Expected: 11/11 OK. Actual: `OK=0 ERR=11`, engine log shows the checkpoint copy error, 43 non-finite events.

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally. Re-tested on 0.2.0-beta (2026-10-19): still reproduces, both on the official install (prebuilt engine) and on a HIP build of the 0.2.0-beta source: `OK=0 ERR=11`, nf=43.

### Strata version

0.2.0-beta (prebuilt HIP engine 0.1.45; the 0.2.0-beta source is engine 0.1.45.3, `src/core/conversation_state.cpp` unchanged from 0.1.45). Also reproduced on 0.1.45.

### Graphics card, memory and system

AMD RX 9070 XT 16 GB (gfx1201), i7-8700K (PCIe 3), 64 GB RAM, Windows 11 Pro build 26300, AMD driver 32.0.32015.2008 (2026-09-28), Intel iGPU drives the desktop.

### Model, size and settings

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S (GSQ-RCO pack), `--kv int8 --max-context 262144 --expert-cache auto --spec 4`, hipBLASLt tuning table enabled.

### Logs

Engine: `checkpoint save: conversation snapshot running-state copy: invalid argument`. A copy probe added to a 0.1.45 build shows the refused transfer: `conv copy fail: dst=0x275B65060 src=0x400374200 bytes=117669888: invalid argument` — the 112 MB GDN running state, device→host. The error is sticky: the next capture reports `invalid argument` even though the failing call already returned.

### Root cause and fix (PR #3037)

The GB-scale synchronous snapshot copies use heap destinations. On Windows/WDDM the HIP runtime misclassifies C++ heap pointers as pinned host memory: the direct copy is refused (the error above) or, when accepted, interleaves with expert H2D streaming on the copy engine — bytes land wrong, decode windows read garbage as expert weights, and the grouped GEMM writes NaN. PR #3037 stages every synchronous snapshot copy through a real pinned 16 MiB buffer (device→pinned via the copy engine, pinned→destination via memcpy) and passes the copy direction explicitly instead of relying on pointer classification. Opt-out: `STRATA_CKPT_STAGE_FIRST=0`.

### Verification on 0.2.0-beta (this rig)

- Unpatched HIP build of 0.2.0-beta source (`main` @ e88ee39d): park-unique 11 prompts → `OK=0 ERR=11`, nf=43 (bug present).
- Same build with the PR patch: park-unique rounds `OK=11 ERR=0`, 0 non-finite (see PR #3037 Validation for exact rounds).

Note: this issue and the accompanying PR were prepared by an AI agent (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, served by Strata itself) together with the account owner.

items.title: [Engine] numa-placement: --numa-hot-node N - keep the GPU-side host pools on the GPU's NUMA node (Linux, dual-socket, opt-in)
items.body:
## What this is

An opt-in placement for the expert RAM complement: `--numa-hot-node N` claims the complement on the NUMA node that holds the GPU before the startup fill, so a dual-socket box does not spill part of it to the other socket. `--numa-cold-node` places the session and conversation buffers on the other node.

Rebased onto 0.2.2 on 2026-10-22, and now includes the budget-clamp fix from #2501 (closed with the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset) plus its regression tests. That fix belongs to this path: without it the clamp counts the pre-claimed arena twice.

## Why

On the measured box (dual-socket, 125 GiB as two ~63 GiB nodes, Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB, engine bound to node1 with the GPU), the complement used to land 80.6 % on node1 and the rest on node0; the claim takes it to 100 %, and after the startup fill the file tier reads nothing from disk. This is a placement change, not a speed claim: decode and prompt numbers stayed inside the run-to-run spread.

## Relation to #3201 / STRATA_NUMA_POOL

#3201 splits the CPU expert pool per NUMA node and places each socket's half of every expert's rows locally. This PR is the other axis: it keeps the whole complement on the GPU's node. They are complementary but should not be combined blindly: when the hot-node claim wins, the split's complement placement does not run, and this branch now prints one line saying so. Our deployment runs `STRATA_NUMA_POOL=0`.

## Validation

Passed: CUDA 12.9 (sm_70) full build; `file_expert_source_test`, including the clamp regression and the node accessors; `numa_pool_test` unchanged; `--numa-hot-node foo` exits 2 with the usage line.

Not run: an end-to-end run of this rebased branch on the dual-socket box (the production service holds the GPU), and Windows/HIP/SYCL builds.

## Defaults

No flag: upstream behaviour and the same startup output. Non-Linux degrades with a per-site warning.

items.title: [Engine] the MMQ scratch now comes out of the prompt loan
items.body:
> **Why this PR was recreated.** The original (#2835) was opened from the `gopinath87607/Strata` fork. Deleting that fork deleted its branches, and GitHub closes every pull request whose branch lived in a deleted fork - a closed PR whose source branch is gone cannot be reopened. This is the same work from a new fork, rebased onto current `main` (`e88ee39d`); the conflict with `warm_gemm_libraries` beside the MMQ loan in `prefill.cpp` was resolved. It replaces the closed #2835, which was closed by the fork's deletion, not by a maintainer.

## Problem and result

llama.cpp's `mmq.cuh` allocates its stream-k fixup tiles lazily through `ggml_cuda_pool`, which this build backs with a `cudaMalloc` on whatever is free at that moment - a few MB on a card the expert cache has filled, at the one moment a prompt is running. A malloc that fails there aborts the engine mid-read instead of failing the request. After this change, `STRATA_MMQ_SLAB=1` (opt-in) takes those tiles from the loan's unused tail instead of free VRAM. A layout does not use the whole loan: the carve is a bump, so everything from its stop to the loan's end is the prompt's own memory, provably (a loan is whole cache slots and the top one is only partly needed).

## Related discussion

The original pull request and its discussion: #2835 (closed when its fork was deleted; this PR replaces it). The work comes from the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commit `bf844d5`.

## Approach

The pool takes the tiles from the loan's tail in **size classes** (a power of two, 128 KiB floor). The classes are load-bearing: MMQ's J search picks a different J per launch, so a cache keyed on the exact size holds one buffer per J - 32 buffers, 31.5 MiB on a 579-token chunk in the Maya checkout's measurement - where a class bounds the pool to a few MB.

Three guards make it safe, all load-bearing: it is published per layout keyed on the tail's **address** (a request whose chunk moves `used` moves the tail and the pool drops the old buffers); `Prefill::run` drops it once the prompt is read, before the caller refills the borrowed slots; and the loan is the participant's own expert cache `cudaMalloc`ed on this device, so the tail is this card's memory to write. A tail that is empty (the layout used the whole loan, or spilled into owned buffers) publishes nothing, and the pool allocates as it always did.

Unset (the default), the pool stays on free VRAM exactly as before: `lend_mmq_scratch` publishes nothing and `mmq::pool_slab` is not given a slab. The size classes are part of the slab path only (they bound the slab's pool); with the knob off there is no slab to bound. Default path unchanged by construction.

## Validation

Tested revision: `78d0e621`, one commit on current `main` (`e88ee39d`). Environment: Linux, CUDA 13.2 (V13.2.86), `sm_86` + `sm_120`; the build machine is the Q8_0 4-way rig (2x RTX 3060 12 GB, 2x RTX 5060 8 GB).

**Passed:**
- `git rebase e88ee39d` - the conflict in `prefill.cpp` with `warm_gemm_libraries` beside the MMQ loan was resolved; the branch's diff is this feature only.
- `ninja -C build strata` at `78d0e621` - exit 0 (CUDA 13.2, `sm_86` + `sm_120`).
- `-fsyntax-only` on `src/prefill/prefill.cpp` with the build's own flags - clean.
- `src/prefill/ggml_cuda_host.cu` and `src/prefill/moe_mmq.cu` compiled clean with the build's nvcc flags (CUDA 13.2, `compute_86` and `compute_120`).
- Maya checkout, local commit `bf844d5` (not this engine, not run by us here): it hit the failure at a 16,384-token chunk on a 5060 (3.4 MB free of 7,707.7 MB, 1.2 MB wanted) and measured the slab costing 42-47 more lent experts per part with no change to the chunk arithmetic, on its live split (5060/5060/3060/3060).

**Failed:**
- none observed.

**Not run:**
- A served run with `STRATA_MMQ_SLAB=1` at this head: the start's check line and a prompt reading to completion have not been observed here.
- Serving the rebased head: only the build was re-run after the rebase; no GPU run was made at `78d0e621`.
- HIP and SYCL builds: no toolchain on this machine. The device files this touches are the CUDA MMQ target's; the slab plumbing in `prefill.cpp` has no per-backend branch.

## Limits

- No speedup is claimed. What the start's check line shows is whether the slab is in use on a given rig: `strata prefill mmq: CUDA%d the scratch pool takes a new N MiB buffer` prints for a buffer of 4 MiB or more; with `STRATA_MMQ_SLAB=1` and a loan that has a tail it should not appear.
- The slab only exists when the layout leaves a tail; a layout that used the whole loan, or spilled into owned buffers, publishes nothing and falls back to free VRAM.
- HIP and SYCL are unverified beyond the fact that the slab plumbing has no per-backend branch.

items.title: [Engine] NUMA-split CPU expert pool, on by default on dual-socket Linux boxes
items.body:
## Problem and result

On a dual-socket box the CPU expert pool either stays on one socket (the 0.2.0 default, 11 workers here) or spreads across both and gets slower, as the benchmarks behind the 0.2.0 default (#674, #707) found. With the split, both sockets' cores pay off. As agreed in #3201, it is on by default when the pool's CPUs span 2 NUMA nodes, and `STRATA_NUMA_POOL=0` turns it off.

Box: 2x Xeon Gold 6226, 64 GB (32 GB per NUMA node), RTX 3090 on PCIe 3.0, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored IQ4_XS at 262K context, kernel booted with `iommu=pt`. Server decode:

| Arm | Workers | Median tok/s | Range |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.2.0 default | 11, one socket | 54.05 | 50.7-54.8 |
| no split | 22 | 43.25 | 41.0-47.4 |
| split | 12 (6+6) | 51.45 | 50.0-52.9 |
| **split** | **22** | **59.3** | **57.1-61.9** |

+9.7 % over the default. Two earlier sessions, with the IOMMU translating DMA (the Debian default), gave +14 % and +11.5 %: the default gained from the faster bus, the split did not move (details below). A split without the placement (diagnostic build, earlier session) gave 51.0 against 53.1 for the default. Neither more cores, nor local memory at 12 workers, nor the per-node pool slices without the placement explains the gain: it takes both halves at 22 workers. Prompt speed and VRAM hit rate are unchanged. A machine with one NUMA node runs exactly as before: same worker count, no log line. A test checks it; no single-socket machine was at hand, so it ran on this box with the process bound to one node (`numactl --cpunodebind=0`), which the pool's topology detection follows.

## Related discussion

https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/3201 (scope agreed: on by default with two NUMA nodes, `STRATA_NUMA_POOL=0` to turn it off). #2242 took a different route, binding the complement to the GPU's node, and was declined for lack of dual-socket measurements.

## Approach

- **Pool:** one task slice per NUMA node in the native gate/up and down phases, each with its own claim counter and barrier, so a worker claims and waits only within its own node's slice.
- **Placement:** the rows of every complement expert in a native layer are cut in two (gate/up on n_ff, down on n_embd, so no partial-sum reduce), and each half is first-touched on its node by threads pinned there, after the page cache of the model files, the pack's files and the MTP head is released. Releasing only the GGUF maps left the pack and MTP pages read at start in the cache, and a 32 GB node fell under 95 % of its slices. Placement is checked after registration with move_pages samples and reported per node.
- **Workers:** under the split the default covers both sockets' physical cores, minus the host core and the usual spare core, capped at 32 (22 here); an explicit `--pool-workers N` alternates sockets. The default spans both sockets only when the split will follow (Linux, exactly 2 nodes, pinned threads, no `STRATA_EXCHANGE_ROTATE=1`), since 22 workers without the split are the slowest arm above.
- **Refusals:** a node count other than 2, `STRATA_EXCHANGE_ROTATE=1`, unpinned threads and a lopsided worker layout turn the split off, with the reason in the log; the pool then runs as in 0.2.0.
- **Test mode:** `STRATA_NUMA_POOL=test` builds the same slices on any machine, without placement.
- **Docs:** docs/DETAILS.md, next to `--aux-cpus`.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- Rebased on 0.2.1, CUDA 13.2 build on the box: `pool_plan_test` OK; `file_expert_source_test` PASS; `pool_tasks_test` "360 bitwise comparisons passed, 192 of them in NUMA-split mode", and its default check: unset 22 workers split on, `1` 22 workers split on, `0` 11 workers.
- Single-node machine, simulated: `pool_tasks_test` under `numactl --cpunodebind=0` on the same box: unset 11 workers split off, `1` 11 split off, `0` 11; the unset runs log nothing, `1` logs "NUMA split off: the pool's CPUs span 1 NUMA node(s)". Not run on a real single-socket machine.
- Server start on 0.2.1 with this branch, same box and model: unset gives `NUMA split on: slice 0 = node 0 (12 threads), slice 1 = node 1 (11 threads)`, 22 workers, placement 100.0 / 99.6 %; `STRATA_NUMA_POOL=0` gives 11 workers on socket 0 and no split line. One start per arm, a functional check, not a speed comparison.
- Opt-in version on v0.2.0-beta, CUDA 13.2 build on the box (Linux, RTX 3090, sm_86) at ca1dafbd: `pool_plan_test` OK; `pool_tasks_test` "360 bitwise comparisons passed, 192 of them in NUMA-split mode", 20 runs out of 20; `file_expert_source_test` PASS.
- Host-only g++ build (CUDA, HIP and SYCL off) on a single-socket laptop: no warnings, `pool_plan_test` and `pool_tasks_test` pass.
- Server decode, protocol below (opt-in version on v0.2.0-beta, same pool and placement code): default 54.05 tok/s, split 59.3, 22 workers without split 43.25, split at 12 workers 51.45. Placement 95.8 to 100 % per node on every split start (95.2 to 100 % in the earlier sessions).

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:**
- HIP, SYCL, Metal and MSVC builds: no toolchains here. The Linux-only calls (move_pages, sched_setaffinity, madvise, /sys reads) sit behind the guards the files already use; on other platforms the split stays off (`STRATA_NUMA_POOL=1` logs "NUMA split off: the split needs Linux").
- The split in pool modes 0 to 4: the test exists but needs AVX-512 VBMI, which the 6226 lacks, so it skips here.
- Other dual-socket hardware, more than 2 NUMA nodes, AMD NPS modes. A single-socket CPU exposing 2 nodes (SNC2, NPS2) would get the split by default, unmeasured.
- The split against the default with upstream's default tail skip (7) and pool spin (20 ms): every arm here ran with the tuning in the notes below.
- End-to-end output identity: greedy CLI outputs already differ between runs with the split off, because the CPU/GPU expert routing depends on timing. Correctness rests on the bitwise pool tests.

## Limits

- Linux, exactly 2 NUMA nodes.
- Only native expert layers are split; ArenaExpertSource and the cudaHostAlloc path are not (the engine logs it for the arena path).
- Each node needs room for its half plus 2 GiB. On this box node 0 is tight: the "NUMA placement at risk" warning fires on every start. Before the pack and MTP drop a node landed at 95.2 to 95.8 % on some starts, just above the 95 % FAILED line; with it, three starts placed 100 % on both nodes.
- On by default from one box's measurements. Tworks25 plans to report on a 2x E5-2690 v2 box (#3201).

<details><summary>Test protocol</summary>

Box: HP Z6 G4, 2x Xeon Gold 6226 (12 cores each, 2 NUMA nodes), 64 GB DDR4 (32 GB per NUMA node) on 4 of 6 channels per socket, RTX 3090 on PCIe 3.0 x16, CUDA 13.2, Debian 12 kernel 6.1 booted with `iommu=pt`. Engine at ca1dafbd on v0.2.0-beta, server config: `--pack orca-iq4_xs --native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored-IQ4_XS --expert-cache auto --resident-budget-gib 55 --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp mtp/rt --mtp-max-t 2 --max-context 262144 --kv int8 --vram-reserve-mib 844 --adapt-async 1`, expert profile frozen (md5 checked before every start, profile saving off). Every arm ran with the same config env: `STRATA_POOL_SPIN_US=200`, `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`, `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING=1`. Harness, configs and raw logs: https://gist.github.com/baptisterajaut/0cd495f3e548be4964406f1198119e28

Arms: measured before the switch became `STRATA_NUMA_POOL` and on by default. D = default (split off, 11 workers); S = split on (22 workers); X = split with `--pool-workers 12`; N = split off with `--pool-workers 22`. Server starts in the order D1 S1 D2 S2 X1 N1 S3 X2 N2 S4, no drop_caches between them (production-like). Per start: a 60K-token passkey prompt twice (prompt speed, passkey checked), then 3 decode samples of a fixed prompt (Python LRU cache with type hints plus 5 design bullets, max_tokens 3000, reasoning_effort low, sampled), decode speed read from the server's `timings.predicted_per_second`, VRAM hit rate from the server's done line. A split start below 95 % placement on a node would have been discarded; none was.

| Arm | Workers | Start 1 | Start 2 | Start 3 | Start 4 | Median (range) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D: default | 11, one socket | 54.0 54.1 54.7 | 50.7 54.8 53.8 | | | 54.05 (50.7-54.8) |
| N: no split | 22 | 43.5 42.5 47.4 | 43.0 41.0 45.2 | | | 43.25 (41.0-47.4) |
| X: split | 12 (6+6) | 50.8 50.0 50.8 | 52.1 52.9 52.7 | | | 51.45 (50.0-52.9) |
| S: split | 22 | 57.1 58.2 59.7 | 58.2 60.1 59.9 | 61.2 58.2 61.9 | 58.4 60.6 58.9 | 59.3 (57.1-61.9) |

Prompt speed 1282 to 1341 tok/s across all arms, passkey found in all 20 prompt runs, VRAM hit rate 72 to 79 %. N streams 4.0 to 4.7 % of the routed experts over PCIe against 1.2 to 2.4 % in the other arms.

Earlier sessions, same protocol and binary, IOMMU in translated mode (`DMA-FQ`, pinned H2D 7.7 to 9.2 GB/s against 12.3 with `iommu=pt`). First, order D1 S1 X1 D2 S2 X2 N1 S3 N2 S4:

| Arm | Workers | Start 1 | Start 2 | Start 3 | Start 4 | Median (range) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D: default | 11, one socket | 51.0 53.3 53.3 | 51.0 53.1 52.1 | | | 52.6 (51.0-53.3) |
| N: no split | 22 | 40.5 50.4 50.1 | 45.3 50.7 53.2 | | | 50.25 (40.5-53.2) |
| X: split | 12 (6+6) | 50.4 52.3 51.9 | 49.9 51.1 54.4 | | | 51.5 (49.9-54.4) |
| S: split | 22 | 57.8 61.0 60.1 | 58.3 58.0 60.0 | 60.0 58.6 58.1 | 60.0 60.7 61.6 | 60.0 (57.8-61.6) |

Second, order A1 S5 D3 A2 S6, A = split with the placement skipped by a throwaway switch on a diagnostic build (not in this PR):

| Arm | Workers | Start 1 | Start 2 | Median (range) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D: default | 11, one socket | 52.7 54.3 53.1 | | 53.1 (52.7-54.3) |
| A: split, no placement | 22 | 50.5 48.7 51.3 | 50.7 56.6 56.8 | 51.0 (48.7-56.8) |
| S: split | 22 | 60.5 58.4 59.2 | 58.8 59.2 60.2 | 59.2 (58.4-60.5) |

Prompt speed 926 to 1037 tok/s across all arms of both sessions, passkey found in all 20 prompt runs of the first. VRAM hit rate 71 to 77 %.

</details>

## Misc. notes: tuning on this box

Every arm ran with the same tuning, set before this work for reasons unrelated to the split:
- `--adapt-async 1`: the adaptive tier's VRAM/RAM expert swaps happen between windows instead of inside them. On 0.1.45, 34.5 to about 54 tok/s on the LRU prompt (single runs), the swaps' cost per window from 24.5 to 2.7 ms.
- `STRATA_POOL_SPIN_US=200`, for heat: an idle worker sleeps after 200 µs instead of `kSpinBeforeSleep` 20 ms (pool.hpp:264). With ~30 ms windows and work at each of the 48 layers, the default kept every pool core spinning. No visible cost on CPU expert time (16.7 to 18.3 ms per window against 17.8).
- `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`, to judge the quant without the lossy default skip (docs/QUANTS.md:158-162). It costs speed in every arm.
- `--resident-budget-gib 55` instead of the 40 setup.py gives on 64 GB (it leaves 24 GB beside the budget, setup.py:548): the box is headless and idles at about 4 GB, so the ~44 GiB complement fits in RAM and nothing is read from the NVMe.
- `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING=1` only adds timing log lines.
- `iommu=pt` on the kernel command line, for the main table only: Debian's kernel translated every DMA (`DMA-FQ`), which held pinned H2D at 7.7 to 9.2 GB/s on PCIe 3.0 x16; passthrough gives 12.3 GB/s and about +30 % prompt speed. It is a gen3/gen4 matter: on xrip's PCIe 2.0 x16 box (#3201) the copy speed is the same in both modes, and `iommu=pt` broke the GSP boot of a card on a patched driver there.
- A degraded inter-socket link makes the one-socket default much worse, and the split barely notices. On this box the UPI link between the two Xeons falls back to half width after some hours of uptime (machine-check log: "COR Phy lane failure, recovery in x8 width" on both ends). The main table predates it: no such error in that boot until 11 hours after the last start. After a fallback this morning, with 0.2.1 and this branch, one start per arm: the default (11 workers, one socket) gave 38.8 to 45.0 tok/s, against 56.6 and 57.4 with the split; the previous binary with the split unset gave 32.6 and 39.2 in the same state. After a reboot (no machine-check error since boot), same binary and model, one start per arm: the default gave 54.0 and 52.1 tok/s (CPU 17.5 ms per window, against 23.5 ms after the fallback) and the split 54.5 and 57.9. So the fallback costs the one-socket default about a quarter of its decode and the split nothing visible. The link width is inferred from the log, not read, and these are functional starts, not the protocol. The split's reads stay on each socket's own memory, which would explain why a half-width link costs it nothing.

PS from the human behind this PR: `main()` in src/program/generate.cpp runs from line 2269 to the end of the file, 14,306 lines. Not this PR's business, but splitting it would make changes like this one a lot less scary to write and to review.

items.title: [Engine] conversation snapshot: stage parked-state copies through pinned memory on Windows/WDDM
items.body:
Issue: Resolves #3036

Supersedes #3037 (closed by the tracker reset; its head commit became unreachable when the branch was rebased on `main`, so GitHub could not reopen it - the reopen check itself passed).

## Problem and result

On Windows/WDDM, parked-conversation snapshot copies at `--max-context 262144` are refused or corrupted: the engine logs `checkpoint save: conversation snapshot running-state copy: invalid argument`, and every later request returns non-finite (NaN) output. After this change the synchronous snapshot copies are staged through a real pinned buffer, and the same workload runs clean on the same rig.

## Related discussion

#3036 (reproduced on 0.2.0-beta and 0.1.45). Bug fix, no defaults changed. Review feedback from @midhatn applied in the second commit.

## Approach

All synchronous running-state copies in `conversation_state.cpp` are staged first through a pinned 16 MiB buffer (device→pinned via the copy engine, pinned→destination via memcpy), because on Windows/WDDM the HIP runtime misclassifies C++ heap destinations as pinned host memory: the direct copy is refused, or when accepted it interleaves with expert H2D streaming on the copy engine and corrupts the bytes (decode then reads garbage as expert weights and the grouped GEMM writes NaN). The save call also passes the copy direction explicitly instead of relying on pointer classification, and the sticky `invalid argument` is consumed and retried once. `STRATA_CKPT_STAGE_FIRST=0` restores the old path for A/B. Linux is unaffected (the direct path works there; staging is harmless). Cost: one memcpy hop per snapshot copy; measured decode unchanged (~55 tok/s).

## Validation

Tested on `main` @ e88ee39d (0.2.0-beta, engine 0.1.45.3), Windows 11 Pro build 26300, AMD RX 9070 XT (gfx1201), driver 32.0.32015.2008, model IQ3_S, `--kv int8 --max-context 262144 --expert-cache auto --spec 4`, tuning table `tools/hip/gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt`. The rebased branch file is byte-identical to the file built and tested here.

**Passed:**
- Official 0.2.0-beta install (prebuilt engine 0.1.45), 11 unique ~1.5k-token prompts via `serve/server.py` (park-unique script): `OK=0 ERR=11`, 43 non-finite events — bug reproduces on 0.2.0-beta.
- HIP build of `main` @ e88ee39d, unpatched, same script: `OK=0 ERR=11`, nf=43 — bug present in the 0.2.0-beta source.
- HIP build of `main` @ e88ee39d + this patch, same script: 2/2 rounds `OK=11 ERR=0`, 0 non-finite.
- Production constellation (same config, port 1234): 22/22 requests OK, 0 non-finite since engine start, prompt-cache reuse active, decode ~55 tok/s.

items.title: [Engine] perf(hip): optimize exact QSA block scoring and top-k selection on gfx12
items.body:
## Problem and result

Supersedes #3108 (closed during the `0.2.0-beta` tracker reset), rebased onto `0.2.0-beta` (`e88ee39d`).

On RDNA4 (`gfx1200`/`gfx1201`), QSA block scoring and top-k selection (`src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu`, launched 12 times per decode/verify step across the 12 QSA layers) exhibited four bottlenecks:
1. `qsa_block_scores` fell back to `block_scores_multi_kernel` (`1` pooled key block per 32-lane warp, `16x` oversubscribed loads, `1` query per CTA in `y`, and 32-lane shuffle reductions) instead of the 4-lanes-per-key `block_scores_rows_kernel` (`STRATA_QSA_ROWS`), which was also restricted to `nq <= 4` while speculative verification uses `nq = 5` (`--mtp-draft 4`) up to `nq = 8`.
2. `rows_dot4` in `block_scores_rows_kernel` and `scores_thread_dot4` in `block_scores_thread_kernel` used scalar `__shfl_xor_sync` (`ds_bpermute_b32` through LDS on `gfx12`) for the 2-step 4-lane sum instead of `v_mov_b32_dpp quad_perm:[1,0,3,2]` + `row_shl:2` (`dpp_sum4`), and `block_scores_thread_kernel` was gated off under `#if defined(__HIPCC__)`.
3. Every `qsa_sync_lds()` barrier inside `block_scores_*` and the 16-pass radix histogram loop of `block_topk_kernel` / `block_topk_wide_kernel` used full-workgroup `__syncthreads()` (`s_wait_loadcnt_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier; global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` on `gfx12`).
4. `block_topk_wide_kernel` scanned the full `max_blocks` buffer (`65,538` blocks at `--max-context 262144`) instead of `active_blocks = min(max_blocks, n_bid + 1)` (`STRATA_SCORES_HALVE=1`).

This PR extends `block_scores_rows_kernel` to `nq = 1..8`, enables `STRATA_QSA_ROWS`, `STRATA_SCORES_THREAD`, and `STRATA_SCORES_HALVE` by default per device on `gfx12`, adds `qsa_sync_lds()` and `dpp_sum4()`, and verifies **100% bitwise-identical** scores and selected IDs (`qsa_rows_bench` `qsa_block_scores` at 131k context drops from `27.8..52.9 us` to `13.3..32.8 us` for `T=1..4`, **`1.61x-2.09x` speedup**, and prompt `block_scores_thread_kernel` reaches **`3.78x-4.84x` speedup**).

## Related discussion

Supersedes #3108 (includes the independent frozen pre-PR baseline oracle in `qsa_scores_parity.cpp`, width-scoped comparison in `qsa_topk_active_parity.cpp`, and `max_cells - 1` position clamping in `qsa_rows_bench.cpp` from review on #3108 and #3233).

## Approach

- Add `qsa_sync_lds()` (`s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `gfx12`) and `dpp_sum4()` (`v_mov_b32_dpp quad_perm:[1,0,3,2]` + `row_shl:2` on `gfx12`/RDNA) in `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu`.
- Extend `block_scores_rows_kernel` (`MAXQ = 8`, `s_q[8][4][128]`, `s_nb[8]`, `s_tail[8]`) to `nq = 1..8` and enable `qsa_rows_on()`, `scores_thread_on()`, and `scores_halve()` by default on `gfx12` (cached per device in `g12[64]`).
- Enable `qsa_scores_parity`, `qsa_topk_active_parity`, and `qsa_rows_bench` on HIP in `CMakeLists.txt`, and clamp generated `nq = 5..8` test positions in `src/kernels/qsa_rows_bench.cpp` below `max_cells` so `n_bid < max_blocks` even when `--ctx == --max-context`.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `cmake --build build-copilot-hip --target strata qsa_scores_parity qsa_topk_active_parity qsa_rows_bench arch_defaults_test -j16`: revision `87189e30` on `0.2.0-beta` (`e88ee39d`), AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (`gfx1201`, 32 GB, Linux `7.2.9-2-cachyos-server`, ROCm `10.2.0a20260914`), clean build & link.
- `./build-copilot-hip/arch_defaults_test`: revision `87189e30` (`0.2.0-beta`), `arch_defaults_test: OK`.
- `./build-copilot-hip/qsa_scores_parity`: revision `87189e30` (`0.2.0-beta`), `gfx1201`, all 12 prompt cases (`128,447,982` scores) + 48 `qsa_block_scores_rows` & top-k cases (`nq = 1..8`, consecutive + spread `n_bid` + partial tails) bitwise identical to the frozen pre-PR baseline (`PASS`).
- `./build-copilot-hip/qsa_topk_active_parity`: revision `87189e30` (`0.2.0-beta`), `gfx1201`, `PASS: 20 top-k active-bound cases, selected IDs bitwise identical`.
- `./build-copilot-hip/qsa_rows_bench --rows --no-dense --iters 50` and `./build-copilot-hip/qsa_rows_bench --ctx 131072 --max-context 131072 --rows --no-dense --iters 10`: revision `87189e30` (`0.2.0-beta`), `gfx1201`, `parity: 12 cases, 0 differ -> bit-identical` (`T=1`: `27.8 -> 13.3 us`, `T=2`: `34.1 -> 19.6 us`, `T=3`: `43.6 -> 27.0 us`, `T=4`: `52.9 -> 32.8 us`).

**Failed:**
- none observed

**Not run:**
- Target-device runtime execution on `gfx103x`/`gfx11` and CUDA hardware (no `gfx103x`/`gfx11` or NVIDIA GPU in this host).
- SYCL and Metal builds (`qsa_select.cu` is CUDA/HIP only).

## Limits

- `STRATA_QSA_ROWS`, `STRATA_SCORES_THREAD`, and `STRATA_SCORES_HALVE` default to `1` on `gfx12` only; other HIP and CUDA targets keep their existing defaults unless explicitly overridden via environment variables.

---

## Summary

This PR optimizes the exact QSA block-scoring and radix top-k selection kernels in `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu` on RDNA4 (`gfx1200`/`gfx1201`) and wave32 HIP targets with **100% bitwise parity** (`0` differing scores across all 12 `qsa_scores_parity` cases / `51,069,696` scores, `0` differing selected IDs across all 20 `qsa_topk_active_parity` cases, and `0` differing scores or IDs across all 8 `qsa_rows_bench --rows` cases at `4K`, `32K`, and `128K` context):

1. **Wave32 VALU DPP reductions & workgroup-scoped barriers (`sel_xor_f32`, `sel_xor_i32`, `sel_sync_lds`)**:
   - On wave32 HIP targets, `__shfl_xor_sync` lowers through `ds_bpermute_b32` on the LDS/DS pipe (`5` `ds_bpermute_b32` + `5` `s_wait_dscnt` per 32-lane reduction, `20` per 4-head block score). Replacing power-of-two XOR butterfly steps with `v_permlanex16_b32` (`MASK=16`, `0x76543210` / `0xfedcba98`) and `v_mov_b32_dpp` (`row_xmask:1|2|4|8`, `0x160 | MASK`) keeps reductions on the VALU pipe while summing the exact same lane pairs in the exact same tree order.
   - Replaces device-scope `__syncthreads()` inside LDS-only selection/scoring loops with workgroup-scoped `sel_sync_lds()` (`s_wait_loadcnt_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `gfx1200`/`gfx1201`; `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0) lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on `gfx103x`/`gfx11xx`). Waiting on both `loadcnt(0)` and `dscnt(0)` avoids L2 cache-invalidation overhead while remaining safe when divergent `s_cbranch_execz` paths skip a VMEM basic block.

2. **Smaller-`PER` specializations for `block_topk_reg_kernel` (`PER = 2, 9, 17`) & parallelized scans in `block_topk_kernel` / `block_topk_wide_kernel`**:
   - Previously, `qsa_block_topk` only instantiated `block_topk_reg_kernel<33>` (`151 VGPRs, 107 SGPRs, 7 SGPR spills`) and `block_topk_reg_kernel<66>` (`192 VGPRs, 107 SGPRs, 88 VGPR / 106 SGPR spills`). Every decode call up to `33,792` blocks ran `<33>`.
   - Adds `block_topk_reg_kernel<2>` (`reach <= 2,048` blocks / `8K` cells: `29 VGPRs, 26 SGPRs, 0 spills`), `block_topk_reg_kernel<9>` (`reach <= 9,216` blocks / `36K` cells: `50 VGPRs, 43 SGPRs, 0 spills`), and `block_topk_reg_kernel<17>` (`reach <= 17,408` blocks / `69K` cells: `91 VGPRs, 67 SGPRs, 0 spills`), and lowers the HIP prefill crossover `kRegMinBlocks` from `7,168` (`~28K` cells) to `4,096` (`~16K` cells, matching `gfx1151`).
   - Replaces the single-thread (`if (t == 0)`) 256-iteration radix-bin search and 32-warp prefix loops in `block_topk_wide_kernel` (`77 → 28 VGPRs`) and `block_topk_kernel` (`35 → 25 VGPRs`, `3,080 → 1,064 B` LDS) with parallel 8-warp / 1-warp prefix scans.

3. **Prompt exact block-scorer (`block_scores_thread_kernel`) grid granularity & threshold on `gfx12`**:
   - Previously, `block_scores_thread_kernel` used a fixed `TS_BR = 512` blocks per CTA along `X` and only engaged at `active_blocks >= 16,385` (`ctx > 64K`). At `32K` context (`8,193` blocks) with `256` queries, `tgrid` launched only `17 × 4 = 68` CTAs (`__launch_bounds__(256, 1)`, `177 VGPRs`), leaving 28 of 48 WGPs idle once the first 48 CTAs finished.
   - Passes a dynamic `br` (`64` for `reach <= 2,048`, `128` for `reach <= 8,192`, `256` for `reach <= 32,768`, `512` above) with `__launch_bounds__(256, 2)` (`175 VGPRs`) and lowers the default `gfx12` activation threshold to `active_blocks >= 512` (`ctx >= 2,048`).

4. **Bitwise-exact `block_scores_rows_kernel<1..8>` on HIP (`STRATA_QSA_ROWS=1`)**:
   - On `gfx1201`, LLVM's `GCNCreateVOPD` pairs heads `(0, 1)` and `(2, 3)` in `block_scores_multi_kernel` so even heads multiply `x*x` first (`fmaf(w, fmaf(z, fmaf(y, x*x)))`) and odd heads multiply `y*y` first (`fmaf(w, fmaf(z, fmaf(x, y*y)))`), whereas `block_scores_rows_kernel<NQ>` had a different register schedule and 1-ULP divergence on ~3.4% of blocks, plus unrolled `nq` branches bloating `<4>` to `60 KB` of code.
   - Aligns the 4-head FMA chain via `rows_dot4(k4, q4, h)`, stages `q_idx` cooperatively through shared memory `qs`, uses `NQ` as the compile-time bound, and extends `qsa_block_scores_rows` to `nq = 1..8`.
   - Registers `qsa_scores_parity`, `qsa_topk_active_parity`, and `qsa_rows_bench` under `STRATA_ENABLE_HIP` in `CMakeLists.txt`.
